title: Priority-aware admission controller with GPU headroom estimator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Under sustained high QPS we observe repeated GC-like KV evictions and GPU OOM near tail spikes, which degrades P95 latency and causes cascading cascade of microbatch rejections. Current admission is a bulk threshold per-worker which does not account for request priority, KV residency pressure, or fragmented GPU headroom.

Goal: Implement an admission controller that combines (1) a lightweight per-GPU headroom estimator (memory usage + fragmentation + estimated KV reinstatement cost) and (2) priority-aware microbatch admission so we can accept high-priority requests at slightly higher cost while shedding low-priority work earlier. The controller should be compatible with continuous batching and support fast dynamic adjustment during QPS bursts without introducing oscillations.

Proposed design summary:
- GPU headroom estimator: rolling-window estimator per device that tracks committed memory, allocator fragmentation delta, and hot KV footprint (estimated resident KV size by namespace). Use exponential smoothing and a short-term linear prediction to estimate available bytes for new activation + KV reinflation. Provide a headroom score in bytes and a confidence band.
- Priority buckets: classify incoming requests into three priority tiers (P0: user-facing interactive paths, P1: background inference with timeliness needs, P2: low-priority batch/async). Each bucket has a configurable soft quota and a minimum guaranteed headroom fraction.
- Admission logic: compute the incremental memory cost of admitting the microbatch (sequence length distribution, kv-lookup count, expected KV pin rate). Admit if: estimated_headroom >= incremental_cost + safety_margin_for_confidence. If not, attempt one of the following in order: 1) reduce microbatch size (floor to 1) and re-evaluate, 2) if admitted and priority higher than lowest, evict non-critical KV segments (LRU-backed per-namespace eviction) to free headroom, 3) otherwise reject the request with indicated retry-after or route to lower-cost model variant.
- Backpressure smoothing: use an adaptive hysteresis controller with separate time constants for increase vs decrease to avoid thrashing during QPS microbursts. Increase smoothing factor when headroom confidence is low.
- Metrics & telemetry: expose headroom_estimate_bytes, headroom_confidence, incremental_cost_estimate, admission_decision (admit/resize/evict/reject), per-priority acceptance rate, P50/P95 latency per-priority, kv_eviction_rate, and memory_fragmentation_delta.

Why different from existing work: this ticket focuses on combining allocator-level fragmentation signals and KV reinflation cost into a live headroom estimator and tying it to per-request priority-aware admission and targeted eviction flows. Existing items focused on microbatch ceilings or general backpressure heuristics; this one explicitly models the cost of KV reinstatement and prioritizes admission paths based on business criticality.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full allocator rewrite, cross-GPU NVLINK redistribution, or new on-disk swap mechanism. This is an admission-layer plus passive KV eviction lever and estimator, not a hardware-level change.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implementation merged behind runtime flag (config: admission_v2.enabled) with feature gating per-cluster.
- Headroom estimator emits metrics at 5s cadence and matches offline simulation within 10% on held-out trace.
- Per-priority admission reduces low-priority rejection spikes: during synthetic high-QPS test (2x baseline) acceptance rate for P0 requests stays >= 98% and P95 latency for P0 does not regress > 15% compared to baseline.
- No regressions in overall GPU OOM rate on canary (<= current OOM rate).
- Dashboard and alerts created: Headroom anomaly alert (headroom_estimate < threshold for >30s) and admission rejection surge alert (>3x baseline for >1m).

Implementation plan and milestones:
1) Week 1: implement headroom estimator prototype in runtime agent; integrate allocator/fragmentation probes (Mmap/allocator hooks) and KV residency counters. Unit tests for estimator math.
2) Week 2: implement admission controller core with priority buckets and microbatch resizing logic; add config knobs for safety_margin and smoothing constants.
3) Week 3: integrate targeted eviction flow (namespace-scoped LRU eviction with soft-deprioritization), add metrics and tracing hooks to identify decision path.
4) Week 4: end-to-end synthetic load tests on staging, compare to offline trace simulator, iterate.
5) Week 5: canary rollout to 5% of hosted clusters, run capture of traces and dashboards, and hold.
6) Week 6: full rollout if metrics pass.

Testing & validation plan:
- Offline simulation: replay production QPS trace and compute estimator error vs true headroom.
- Microbench harness: run QPS ramp scenarios with mixed priorities and heavy KV hot set churn; validate P0 SLOs.
- Fault injection: artificially increase fragmentation and KV reinflation cost, verify admissions respond by resizing/evicting rather than causing OOM.
- Replay acceptance log: store decision logs and replay in isolation to ensure deterministic behavior for a given sequence.

Rollout and rollback notes:
- Feature gated. Canary to 5% then 20% before full. Immediate rollback if P0 acceptance falls below 97% or OOM rate increases by >10% on canary.

Dependencies:
- KV metrics exports (ENG-24109) for precise resident size counters or fallback to approximations.
- Runtime allocator probe API (allocator-team) to report fragmentation deltas.
- Dashboard and alerting tickets (linked below).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: estimator underestimates reinflation cost causing optimistic admissions -> mitigation: conservative default safety_margin and confidence-based throttling.
- Risk: eviction thrash harming tail latency when many small evictions occur -> mitigation: batch evictions and prefer larger-scoped namespace-level evictions with cooldown.
- Risk: oscillation during highly spiky QPS -> mitigation: asymmetric hysteresis and increased smoothing during low confidence windows.

Deliverables:
- Runtime change (C++/Rust) + unit tests behind flag.
- Admission feature flag and config docs.
- Grafana dashboard and alert rules.
- Load test scripts and simulation results.
